Maintenance Procedures Information System
Introduction

This document was produced in 1999 in English under No. T-SS-005-r0 and was translated into Arabic under No. T-005-r1a. It shows the technical inspection checklist for 125 MVA power transformers, denoted by the letter I1, to be carried out monthly, denoted by the letter Y1, according to the manufacturer's instructions and acquired experience, in order to provide safety factors for personnel and to maintain the safe operation of the equipment.
Safety Precautions
Issue a work order approved by the competent authority.
Isolate the transformer and apply suitable earths on all sides
Wear a helmet, shoes and a safety belt.
Beware of falling into the oil collection pit when working on large power transformers
Use fiberglass ladders, well secured, when climbing onto the transformer
The use of metal ladders is forbidden.
Tools, Equipment and Instruments Used
Helmet, shoes and safety belt
Fiberglass ladders
Work steps to be carried out
1. Check for any oil leakage and treat it if found.
2. Inspect the transformer paint and repaint any place where there is rust.
3. Inspect the condition of the earthing switch and retighten all the connection bolts.
4. Clean the bushings.
5. Check the oil level in all bushings.

6. Open the bleed valve of the gas protection device (Buchholz) until a small amount of oil comes out, and test the alarm and trip circuits using the push button located after the vent valve, and retighten all the electrical connections.
7. Inspect the condition of the silica gel and replace it if necessary.
8. Inspect the pressure relief device (Pressure Relief Valve) for the main transformer and the tap changer, if fitted.

9. Inspect the condition of the cooling fans and make sure the fan protection screens are clean and free of any obstructions. Inspect the fan blades. Inspect the drive motors of all the fans and make sure there is no abnormal noise from the bearings. It is recommended to replace the bearings after 3000 operating hours or 4 years, whichever comes first.
10. Inspect the transformer operating cabinet and clean it of dust. Inspect the door gasket. Retighten all electrical connections. Inspect the heaters and make sure they are working properly.

11. Clean the transformer and the oil coolers using pressurized water, and do not direct the water stream directly onto the fans. It is recommended to use the transformer fire fighting system during the cleaning process to test the operation of the fire fighting system at the same time.

12. Carry out the winding insulation resistance test and record the readings (megger readings): high-voltage windings to low-voltage windings – high-voltage windings to the tertiary winding – low-voltage windings to the tertiary winding – high-voltage windings to earth – low-voltage windings to earth – tertiary winding to earth, and compare these readings with the previous readings.
13. Carry out the dissipation factor test (Dissipation factor tan δ) and compare the results with the previous results for the transformer.
14. Carry out the winding ratio test (Ratio test) and record the readings on the test data recording form attached to the document, and compare the results with the previous tests.

15. A- Record the winding resistance readings and compare them with the previous readings. B- Inspect and clean the tap changer operating cabinet, check the tightness of the electrical connections, inspect the heaters and make sure they are working properly. Inspect the door gasket and make sure it closes tightly, and test the operation of the mechanism motor.

16. Operate the tap changer through a complete cycle from the highest step to the lowest step and then return it to the step it was on during operation, in order to clean the internal contacts of the tap changer from the carbon deposited on them.
17. Inspect the tap changer drive shaft and retighten the bolts of all connections.
18. Record the last reading on the tap changer operation counter.
19. Take samples of the oil from the main transformer tank as well as from the tap changer to send them for laboratory analysis (see document T-001-r0).
20. Make sure there are no tools, equipment or cleaning cloths left on the transformer.
21. Return the transformer to normal operating condition after the approval of the control centre.
